agentClaim.summary: Audited every major claim in the critic report (asgn_p05_2_r7_proof_driver_op_006) against the frozen mdview case context and the observed working-directory evidence. Most claims are grounded. One process claim (PROC-2) is contradicted by evidence the critic explicitly declined to read: op_002/op_003/op_004's own assignment.json files each embed the identical explicit inline-editing constraint paragraph, so the constraint is not enforced 'only at the critic stage' as claimed. One risk item (path traversal on the write route) is a generic addition not traceable to any text in the frozen brief.
agentClaim.methodology: For each major claim: (1) checked whether it is a direct quote/paraphrase of the frozen case brief embedded verbatim in op_006/assignment.json; (2) checked whether it is a direct, verifiable read of a working-directory file (run.json/stderr.log/stdout.log/assignment.json); (3) where the critic made a claim about parts of the pipeline it explicitly said it did not read (op_002/003/004), independently read those files to verify the claim rather than taking it on faith.

claims.claim: op_005/runs/01/run.json shows status=failed, exitCode=1, artifacts=[]; stderr.log shows quota error; stdout.log empty; agent-report.md/agent-result.json do not exist; assignment.json shows dispatchedRuns=["01"], maxRuns=1.
claims.basis: Directly verifiable from the named files in the working directory; independently re-read and confirmed identical content.

claims.claim: Zero clusters, zero named findings, and zero candidate answer text reached the critic stage.
claims.basis: Direct logical consequence of C1 (op_005 is the critic's sole contextRef and it produced no artifacts).

claims.claim: The inline-editing check is 'not-evaluable', not a clean pass, and must not be read downstream as 'no violation found'.
claims.basis: Follows directly from C2: with no candidate answer text available, no check could have run. This is a valid, non-speculative inference from the evidence.

claims.claim: The critic stage was dispatched over a failed producer stage with only op_005 as its authorized input, so a critic fed an empty input set can only return 'nothing to flag', indistinguishable from 'checked and clean'; the dependency should be hard.
claims.basis: op_006/assignment.json contextRefs=["asgn_p05_2_r7_proof_driver_op_005"] confirmed; op_005 confirmed failed with no artifacts (C1). The structural observation is accurate; the recommendation is a reasonable, clearly-labeled opinion built on grounded facts.

claims.claim: The inline-editing constraint 'has no independent enforcement point' and is 'enforced only at the critic stage'; any upstream failure 'silently disables the constraint check entirely'.
claims.basis: Contradicted by directly available evidence the critic explicitly chose not to read (§5, 'Scope discipline'). Independently reading op_002/assignment.json, op_003/assignment.json, and op_004/assignment.json shows each explorer's own objective embeds the identical verbatim paragraph: 'Any candidate answer that proposes inline editing on the existing view screen has NOT answered the locked objective and must be flagged as such, never silently accepted.' The constraint is delivered to every stage of the pipeline, not introduced only at the critic. The critic cannot know whether explorer-level compliance held (it never read those outputs), but the specific claim that the constraint has 'no independent enforcement point' upstream is an overclaim built on an intentional evidence gap, not on what the working directory actually contains.

claims.claim: Failure cause is infrastructural: provider quota exhaustion (executorId=agy-cli, providerModel=gemini, model=gemini-3.1-pro-low), not analytical.
claims.basis: Directly quoted from op_005/runs/01/run.json and stderr.log, independently confirmed.

claims.claim: Any sibling stage routed to the same provider/model in the same window is exposed identically; a rerun without a fallback or wait 'will most likely reproduce the same exit code'.
claims.basis: Plausible engineering inference, but nothing in the working directory shows which provider/model other stages (op_002-004, or a rerun of op_005) are routed to, or that the quota is shared rather than per-stage/per-key. Presented as near-certain ('will most likely') without evidence of the routing config.

claims.claim: The R3 minority-preservation requirement is unverifiable for this run because the clusterer produced nothing.
claims.basis: op_005/assignment.json explicitly names 'this framework's own R3 requirement' for preserving a 1-of-3 dissenting explorer view; combined with C1 (no clusterer output exists), the conclusion that this requirement is currently unverifiable is directly supported.

claims.claim: Any cluster proposing edits grafted onto the existing view route, an edit-mode toggle, or contenteditable on rendered output should be flagged as not answering the objective; a same-handler disguised editor is an evasion of the same constraint.
claims.basis: Directly derived from the objective's own explicit constraint text (verbatim, quoted identically in op_006/assignment.json) prohibiting inline editing on the existing view screen.

claims.location: checklist / claims needing evidence – FileStore port
claims.claim: 'Architecturally simple' asserted without naming which layer absorbs writes is unsupported; PRD §7.4 defines a FileStore port whose read-only-ness at the trait level is a code fact to check, not assume.
claims.basis: §7.4 of the frozen brief verbatim defines PORTS including 'FileStore' and states the dependency rule; the critic correctly refrains from asserting whether it is read-only, framing it as unresolved rather than inventing an answer.

claims.location: checklist / claims needing evidence – desktop adapter
claims.claim: Any claim the desktop adapter is unaffected ignores §7.5's explicit read-only invariant; an editor reachable through the Tauri webview at :7700 still touches it.
claims.basis: §7.5 verbatim states desktop is read-only; §7.1 verbatim states the webview attaches at ':7700'. Both facts are quoted correctly and combined validly.

claims.location: checklist / claims needing evidence – single-daemon concurrency
claims.claim: Single-daemon topology making concurrency 'trivial' ignores that §7.1's two-daemon prohibition says nothing about two browser tabs editing the same file through one daemon.
claims.basis: §7.1 verbatim forbids two daemons writing one SQLite registry; the critic's distinction (registry-level guarantee vs. file-content-level concurrency) is a valid, non-fabricated reading of the same text.

claims.location: checklist / risks – lost update / concurrent edit
claims.claim: The notify watcher plus live-reload WebSocket means an external editor's save and a browser save can race; no conflict-detection story exists in the frozen PRD.
claims.basis: Both components cited ('notify impl Watcher' in §7.4, '/ws WebSocket endpoint (live reload)' in §7.2) are real elements of the frozen brief; the race-condition risk is a reasonable synthesis of two real facts, not an invented one, and the absence of a conflict story is accurate (no such mechanism appears anywhere in the quoted brief).

claims.claim: Atomic replace vs in-place truncate, newline/CRLF/encoding preservation, and partial-write behavior are unaddressed risks.
claims.basis: Generic software-engineering risk that applies to any file-writing feature; nothing in the frozen brief discusses file encoding, write strategy, or newline handling. Reasonable to raise, but not traceable to the given context — it is domain knowledge applied to the objective's bare requirement to 'write changes back', not a context-grounded finding.

claims.claim: §3.2 states MDView is explicitly not an authoring tool/WYSIWYG editor and desktop is read-only, not an editor; adding an editor is a non-goal reversal and a maintainer decision, not a technical detail.
claims.basis: Verbatim quote match against §3.2 of the frozen brief ('Không phải authoring tool hay WYSIWYG editor', 'vẫn read-only, không phải editor').

claims.claim: §3.2 waives authentication on the grounds of read-only local/private-network use; a write endpoint invalidates that premise, making an unauthenticated writable daemon on :7700 materially riskier than an unauthenticated reader.
claims.basis: §3.2 verbatim ties the no-auth decision to simplicity/read-only assumptions; §7.1 verbatim gives the ':7700' port. The inference that a write capability changes the risk calculus of an already-stated design decision is sound and directly tied to quoted text.

claims.claim: A safe read route does not imply a safe write route; path traversal on the write route specifically should be checked.
claims.basis: Nothing in the frozen brief discusses path resolution, sanitization, or traversal risk on any route (read or write). This is a standalone generic security consideration imported from outside the given context, not derived from it.

claims.claim: A write triggers notify → re-index → live reload, which can clobber or churn the editor's own buffer.
claims.basis: Both mechanisms (notify-based watcher, WebSocket live reload) are named directly in §7.2/§7.4 of the frozen brief; the feedback-loop risk is a valid mechanical consequence of chaining two real, cited features.

claims.claim: §3.2 excludes sync/backup, so a bad write to a source .md file has no in-product undo.
claims.basis: Verbatim quote match: '§3.2, Non-goals – Không sync hay backup files.'

claims.claim: comrak parses markdown for display; round-tripping edited text through an AST-based path risks silently reformatting the user's source.
claims.basis: §7.4 verbatim names 'render (comrak)' as the render engine in mdview-core; the round-tripping/reformatting risk is a standard, directly-applicable consequence of that named tool being AST-based, not an invented detail.

claims.claim: The critic did not read op_002/op_003/op_004 because those are op_005's inputs, not the critic's, and reading them would collapse stage independence.
claims.basis: Verifiable behavioral claim about the critique itself: neither the agent-report.md nor agent-result.json for op_006 cite any content from op_002/003/004 beyond their existence, consistent with the stated abstention. The independence argument is a defensible process principle, not a factual claim needing external evidence.

claims.claim: Re-run op_005 before re-running the critic; record the inline-editing constraint as UNVERIFIED, not passed; make the critic hard-depend on a non-empty clusterer artifact.
claims.basis: These are recommendations, not empirical claims; each follows directly from the grounded findings in C1-C4 and C8, and none of them assert anything about content the critic did not have.

aggregateFindings.keyIssue: PROC-2 (C5) is the most consequential unsupported claim: it makes a definitive negative statement ('no independent enforcement point', 'enforced only at the critic stage') about parts of the pipeline the critique explicitly declined to inspect, and that statement is directly contradicted by the actual contents of op_002/op_003/op_004's assignment.json files, which all carry the identical explicit constraint text given to the critic itself.
aggregateFindings.secondaryIssue: PROC-3's recurrence prediction (C7) and two checklist risk items (C14 write-back safety, C17 path traversal) are reasonable engineering additions but are not traceable to anything in the frozen case brief or the observed evidence — they are imported general risk knowledge, not context-grounded findings. This does not make them wrong, only unverified against the frozen record this audit was scoped to check.

unresolvedQuestions: Does the framework intend explorer-level self-flagging of the inline-editing constraint to count as 'enforcement', or is critic-stage flagging the only enforcement point that counts by design? This determines whether PROC-2's underlying concern (single point of failure) survives even after correcting its overclaim about text-level presence.
